blocks.text: Managing Google Docs for virtual assistants on Mac

As a virtual assistant, you likely manage documents for several clients at once. Since Google Docs lives in the browser, you need a strategy to keep these documents separate. Use browser profiles in Chrome or Safari to keep client accounts distinct. This prevents you from accidentally sharing a document from one client with another.

Once you have your profiles set up, focus on speed. Learning the keyboard shortcuts is the most effective way to reduce the time you spend on manual formatting. On a Mac, the ⌘ key is your best friend. It replaces the Ctrl key from Windows machines.
Essential Google Docs keyboard shortcuts for Mac

Every second counts when you are billing by the hour. Memorizing these shortcuts will make your document creation much faster. If you forget a shortcut, you can press ⌘ + / to open the full list inside your document.

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you navigate Google Docs without hunting through menus. When you need to find a specific setting, hold ⌥ + ⌘ and ask Lazur. Lazur will point at the menu item on your screen. This is helpful when you are working in a complex document and cannot remember where a specific feature is hidden.
Handling large documents and file limits

You might occasionally work on massive documents. Remember that a single Google Doc has a limit of 1.02 million characters. If you reach this limit, you must split your content into separate files. For non-Google files like PDFs, you can upload up to 5 TB to your Google Drive, provided you have the storage space.

Keep your Drive organized using a consistent naming convention. Include the date and the client name in the file title. For example, use YYYY-MM-DD-ClientName-ProjectName. This makes searching for files much faster when you are in a rush.
Use the table of contents feature for any document over five pages. This helps your clients navigate your work easily. You can insert one by going to Insert > Table of Contents in the top menu.

If you see an error message, start by refreshing your browser tab. If that fails, clear your cache and cookies. Conflicts with browser extensions are a common cause of errors in Google Docs. Try opening the document in an incognito or private window to see if the problem persists.

You can continue working even if your internet connection drops. You must use the Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge browser. Install the Google Docs Offline extension from the Chrome Web Store. Once enabled, turn on offline access in your Google Drive settings. This syncs your files locally so you do not lose progress.

faq.question: Is there a native Google Docs app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, there is no official standalone app. You access Google Docs through a web browser like Chrome or Safari.

faq.question: How do I add a comment using the keyboard?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ + ⌥ + M while your cursor is in the document to instantly open the comment box.

faq.question: Can I work on Google Docs without an internet connection?
faq.answer: Yes, but you must be using Chrome or Edge and have the Google Docs Offline extension installed.

faq.question: What should I do if Google Docs is running slowly?
faq.answer: Clear your browser cache and cookies. Check for conflicting extensions and ensure you are using the latest version of your browser.
